label: early fresh p/a/y/k-type input in sequences starting with n/x/u/g/i/h
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (98% of mass), mostly at positions 2-5 and peaking at t=3. It never fires at t=0, and the copy phase is essentially silent; there is a weak tail at the delimiter. Activation looks additive. One part is the current input token: p and a are strongest (about 8x lift, 57% of mass together), then y, k, 1, f, b, j. The other part is sequence context: a first token from n/x/u/g/i/h (also 2/v) raises it, as does seeing more of those tokens earlier. The top activations (near max) are p or a at t=4 after a prefix such as n x .. or x n ... It fires mostly on the first occurrence of the input token (95% of mass). The same p/a inputs without that kind of prefix are often inactive, so precision is limited (about 0.35). No crisp boolean rule captures the graded sum: dev F1 is about 0.45 and mass recall 0.72.
